questions.q: The law of conservation of mass was put forward by
questions.explanation: Lavoisier showed that in a chemical reaction the total mass of reactants equals the total mass of products.

questions.q: Which law states that a pure chemical compound always contains the same elements combined in the same proportion by mass?
questions.explanation: This is the law of definite (constant) proportions, given by Proust.

questions.q: How many molecules are present in 4.4 g of carbon dioxide? (C = 12, O = 16; NA = 6.022 × 10^23 per mol)
50 mL of 2 M HCl is diluted with water to a final volume of 100 mL. What is the new molarity?
A hydrocarbon has the empirical formula CH and a molar mass of 78 g/mol. What is its molecular formula? (C = 12, H = 1)
questions.explanation: The empirical formula mass is 13, and 78/13 = 6, so the molecular formula is C6H6.

questions.q: Ethene burns as C2H4 + 3O2 → 2CO2 + 2H2O. What mass of oxygen is needed to burn 2.8 g of ethene completely? (C = 12, H = 1, O = 16)
questions.explanation: 2.8 g of C2H4 (28 g/mol) is 0.1 mol, which needs 0.3 mol O2 = 0.3 × 32 = 9.6 g.

questions.q: What is meant by a limiting reagent in a chemical reaction?
questions.answer: The limiting reagent is the reactant that is completely consumed first and therefore decides the maximum amount of product formed.
keyPoints: It limits the amount of product
questions.explanation: Once the limiting reagent is exhausted, the reaction stops even if other reactants remain.

questions.q: 6 g of hydrogen react with excess nitrogen according to N2 + 3H2 → 2NH3. Calculate the mass of ammonia formed. (N = 14, H = 1)
questions.explanation: The mole ratio H2 : NH3 is 3 : 2, so 3 mol of H2 yields 2 mol of NH3 weighing 34 g.

questions.q: Isotopes of an element have the same
questions.explanation: Isotopes have the same atomic number (protons) but different numbers of neutrons, and so different mass numbers.

questions.q: Cathode rays are streams of
questions.explanation: Thomson's experiments with discharge tubes showed that cathode rays consist of negatively charged electrons.

questions.q: How many unpaired electrons are present in a nitrogen atom (Z = 7) in its ground state?
questions.explanation: The configuration 1s2 2s2 2p3 has three 2p electrons occupying separate orbitals with parallel spins (Hund's rule).

questions.q: According to the Aufbau principle, after the 3p orbitals are filled, the next orbital to be filled is
questions.explanation: The 4s orbital has lower energy than 3d (lower n + l value, or n + l equal and lower n), so it fills first.

questions.q: The de Broglie wavelength of a particle of mass m moving with velocity v is
questions.explanation: de Broglie related wavelength to momentum by λ = h/(mv).

questions.q: Heisenberg's uncertainty principle implies that
options: electrons move in fixed circular orbits
the exact position and the exact momentum of an electron cannot both be known simultaneously
questions.explanation: The product of the uncertainties in position and momentum is at least h/4π, which rules out sharply defined electron orbits.

questions.q: Calculate the de Broglie wavelength of an electron moving at 1.0 × 10^6 m/s. (m = 9.1 × 10^-31 kg, h = 6.626 × 10^-34 J s)
questions.explanation: Substituting gives 6.626 × 10^-34 / 9.1 × 10^-25 = 7.28 × 10^-10 m, comparable to atomic dimensions.

questions.q: State Hund's rule of maximum multiplicity and illustrate it with the 2p electrons of nitrogen.
questions.answer: Electrons fill degenerate orbitals singly with parallel spins before any orbital gets a second electron; in nitrogen the three 2p electrons occupy 2px, 2py and 2pz separately.
keyPoints: Degenerate orbitals are filled singly first
Singly occupied electrons have parallel spins
questions.explanation: Keeping electrons apart reduces repulsion and gives a lower energy, more stable arrangement.

questions.q: In the modern long form of the periodic table, the noble gases are placed in
questions.explanation: The noble gases form group 18, with complete outer shells.

questions.q: The transition elements belong to which block of the periodic table?
questions.explanation: In transition elements the last electron enters a d subshell, so they form the d-block.

questions.q: Which of the following elements has the highest electronegativity?
questions.explanation: Fluorine is the most electronegative element on the Pauling scale (about 4.0).

questions.q: Which pair of elements shows a diagonal relationship?
questions.explanation: Lithium (group 1, period 2) resembles magnesium (group 2, period 3) in several properties because of similar charge/size ratios.

questions.q: An element X has the electronic configuration [Ne] 3s2 3p4. Which statement about X is correct?
options: It is a metal belonging to group 14
It is a non-metal that forms a basic oxide
It forms an acidic oxide and its common simple ion is X2-
questions.explanation: Six valence electrons put X in group 16 (sulphur); non-metal oxides such as SO2 are acidic, and X gains 2 electrons to form X2-.

questions.q: Which of the elements Be, B, C and N has the highest first ionisation enthalpy?
questions.explanation: Across period 2 the ionisation enthalpy generally rises with increasing nuclear charge, and nitrogen also has a stable half-filled 2p subshell.

questions.q: Why do the elements of a group show similar chemical properties?
questions.answer: All elements in a group have the same number of electrons in the outermost shell, and chemical behaviour is decided by valence electrons.
keyPoints: Properties change gradually with increasing size
questions.explanation: For example, all alkali metals have ns1 configuration and form +1 ions.

questions.q: Arrange Na, Mg, Al and Si in increasing order of metallic character and give the reason.
questions.answer: Si < Al < Mg < Na. Metallic character decreases across a period as ionisation enthalpy increases and the tendency to lose electrons falls.
keyPoints: Ionisation enthalpy rises across the period
Less tendency to lose electrons going left to right
questions.explanation: Sodium loses its single outer electron most readily, so it is the most metallic.

questions.q: In which of the following species is a coordinate (dative) covalent bond present?
questions.explanation: In NH4+ the lone pair on nitrogen is donated to H+, forming a coordinate bond.

questions.q: Ionic compounds generally have high melting points mainly because of
options: weak van der Waals forces between molecules
strong electrostatic attraction between oppositely charged ions in the lattice
the presence of discrete covalent molecules
questions.explanation: A great deal of energy is needed to overcome the strong electrostatic forces holding ions in the crystal lattice.

questions.q: How many lone pairs of electrons are present on the oxygen atom in a water molecule?
questions.explanation: Oxygen has six valence electrons; two are used in O-H bonds, and the remaining four form two lone pairs.

questions.q: What is the hybridisation of phosphorus in PCl5?
questions.explanation: Five bond pairs around P need five hybrid orbitals, which is sp3d with a trigonal bipyramidal shape.

questions.q: Which sequence shows the carbon-carbon bond lengths in increasing order?
questions.explanation: A higher bond order draws the nuclei closer, so the triple bond is shortest and the single bond is longest.

questions.q: Why does the He2 molecule not exist under normal conditions?
options: Its bond order is zero because bonding and antibonding orbitals are both filled
Helium atoms are too heavy to combine
questions.explanation: Four electrons fill the σ1s and σ*1s orbitals, so bond order = (2 - 2)/2 = 0 and there is no net bonding.

questions.q: Draw (describe) the Lewis structure of carbon dioxide.
questions.answer: O=C=O: carbon in the centre is doubly bonded to each oxygen, and each oxygen carries two lone pairs.
keyPoints: Carbon double bonded to each oxygen
Each oxygen has two lone pairs
questions.explanation: Total valence electrons are 4 + 6 + 6 = 16, shared as two double bonds and four lone pairs.

questions.q: NF3 has a much smaller dipole moment than NH3 even though fluorine is more electronegative than hydrogen. Explain.
questions.answer: In NH3 the bond dipoles point toward nitrogen, in the same direction as the lone-pair dipole, so they add; in NF3 the bond dipoles point toward fluorine, opposite to the lone-pair dipole, so they partly cancel.
keyPoints: NH3: N-H bond dipoles and lone-pair dipole reinforce
NF3: N-F bond dipoles oppose the lone-pair dipole
Net dipole moment is therefore smaller in NF3
questions.explanation: The direction of the bond dipoles relative to the lone pair determines the net dipole, not just the electronegativity difference.

questions.q: Which type of intermolecular force is present in all molecules, including non-polar ones?
questions.explanation: Temporary induced dipoles give dispersion forces in every molecule; the other forces need ions or permanent dipoles.

questions.q: The boiling point of a liquid is the temperature at which its vapour pressure becomes equal to
questions.explanation: Boiling starts when vapour bubbles can form against the external pressure, so vapour pressure equals external pressure.

questions.q: On heating a liquid, its viscosity generally
questions.explanation: Molecules gain kinetic energy and overcome intermolecular forces more easily, so the liquid flows more readily.

questions.q: 10 L of hydrogen and 10 L of methane at the same temperature and pressure contain
questions.explanation: By Avogadro's law equal volumes of gases at the same T and P contain equal numbers of molecules.

questions.q: What is the value of the compressibility factor Z for an ideal gas?
questions.explanation: Z = PV/nRT, which equals 1 at all pressures for an ideal gas.

questions.q: What is the density of carbon dioxide at 273 K and 1 atm? (Molar mass 44 g/mol; molar volume 22.4 L/mol)
questions.explanation: Density = molar mass / molar volume = 44/22.4 = 1.96 g/L.

questions.q: When a gas in a rigid container is heated, its pressure rises because
options: the molecules move faster and hit the walls more often and with greater force
questions.explanation: According to kinetic theory, pressure comes from molecular collisions with the wall, and a higher temperature means a higher average kinetic energy.

questions.q: What is the critical temperature of a gas?
questions.answer: It is the temperature above which a gas cannot be liquefied however high the pressure applied.
keyPoints: Highest temperature at which liquefaction is possible
Above it only the gaseous state exists
Critical pressure is the pressure needed at that temperature
questions.explanation: Above the critical temperature the kinetic energy of molecules is too high for attractions to hold them as a liquid.

questions.q: 0.5 g of a gas occupies 0.25 L at 300 K and 2 atm. Calculate its molar mass. (R = 0.0821 L atm K^-1 mol^-1)
questions.explanation: Using M = wRT/PV gives 0.5 × 24.63 / 0.5 = 24.6 g/mol.

questions.q: The heat exchanged by a system at constant pressure is equal to the change in its
questions.explanation: By definition, qp = ΔH for a process at constant pressure when only pressure-volume work is possible.

questions.q: What is the standard enthalpy of formation of O2(g) in its standard state?
questions.explanation: By convention the standard enthalpy of formation of an element in its most stable form is zero.

questions.q: Which of the following is a state function?
options: Heat absorbed in a given path
questions.explanation: Internal energy depends only on the state of the system, whereas heat and work depend on the path.

questions.q: At equilibrium the Gibbs energy change ΔG of a reaction is
questions.explanation: At equilibrium there is no net driving force, so ΔG = 0.

questions.q: Bond enthalpies are H-H 436, Cl-Cl 243 and H-Cl 431 kJ/mol. What is ΔH for H2(g) + Cl2(g) → 2HCl(g)?
questions.explanation: ΔH = bonds broken - bonds formed = (436 + 243) - 2(431) = 679 - 862 = -183 kJ.

questions.q: How much heat is needed to raise the temperature of 100 g of water from 25 °C to 35 °C? (specific heat of water = 4.18 J g^-1 K^-1)
An ideal gas expands freely into a vacuum in an insulated container. Which statement is correct?
options: Work done is zero and the temperature stays constant
The temperature of the gas rises
questions.explanation: With no external pressure w = 0, and with no heat exchange q = 0, so ΔU = 0; for an ideal gas this means the temperature is unchanged.

questions.q: Distinguish between an exothermic and an endothermic reaction with the sign of ΔH and one example of each.
questions.answer: An exothermic reaction releases heat and has negative ΔH, for example combustion of methane; an endothermic reaction absorbs heat and has positive ΔH, for example decomposition of calcium carbonate.
questions.explanation: The sign of ΔH tells whether the products have lower or higher enthalpy than the reactants.

questions.q: Ice melts at 273 K with an enthalpy of fusion of 6.01 kJ/mol. Calculate the entropy change for melting 1 mol of ice.
keyPoints: At the melting point ΔG = 0, so ΔS = ΔH/T
questions.explanation: At the equilibrium temperature of a phase change, TΔS equals ΔH.

questions.q: The numerical value of the equilibrium constant of a reaction depends on
questions.explanation: For a given reaction K changes only with temperature.

questions.q: A catalyst added to a reaction at equilibrium
options: shifts the equilibrium to the right
shifts the equilibrium to the left
speeds up forward and backward reactions equally without changing Kc
questions.explanation: A catalyst lowers the activation energy for both directions equally, so equilibrium is reached faster but not changed.

questions.q: What is the conjugate base of the hydrogen sulphate ion, HSO4-?
questions.explanation: A conjugate base is formed by removing a proton, and HSO4- minus H+ gives SO4 2-.

questions.q: What is the hydroxide ion concentration of a solution with pH = 9 at 25 °C?
Which of the following is a Lewis acid?
questions.explanation: BF3 has an incomplete octet and accepts an electron pair; NH3, H2O and OH- donate pairs.

questions.q: In the Haber process N2 + 3H2 ⇌ 2NH3, increasing the pressure at constant temperature shifts the equilibrium
options: nowhere, since pressure has no effect
to the right, because there are fewer moles of gas on the right
to the right, because the reaction is endothermic
questions.explanation: Four moles of gas become two, so by Le Chatelier's principle higher pressure favours the side with fewer gas molecules.

questions.q: The solubility product Ksp of AgCl is 1.8 × 10^-10 at 25 °C. What is its molar solubility in pure water?
Why is an aqueous solution of sodium acetate basic?
questions.answer: The acetate ion is the conjugate base of a weak acid and reacts with water: CH3COO- + H2O ⇌ CH3COOH + OH-, producing excess OH- ions.
keyPoints: Salt of weak acid and strong base
questions.explanation: Because [OH-] exceeds [H+], the solution has pH above 7.

questions.q: Calculate the pH of 0.1 M acetic acid solution. (Ka = 1.8 × 10^-5; assume the dissociation is small)
questions.explanation: For a weak acid, [H+] = sqrt(Ka C) when dissociation is much less than the total concentration.

questions.q: A reducing agent is a substance that
options: loses electrons and is itself oxidised
gains electrons and is itself reduced
decreases the oxidation number of itself
questions.explanation: A reducing agent donates electrons to another species, so its own oxidation number increases.

questions.q: What is the oxidation number of oxygen in hydrogen peroxide, H2O2?
questions.explanation: With each H at +1, the two oxygen atoms share -2, so each is -1 (a peroxide).

questions.q: What is the oxidation number of chlorine in HClO4?
What is the average oxidation state of iron in Fe3O4?
questions.explanation: 3x + 4(-2) = 0 gives x = +8/3; it is a mixed oxide of one Fe2+ and two Fe3+.

questions.q: Which metal will displace copper from a copper sulphate solution?
questions.explanation: Zinc is above copper in the activity series and so reduces Cu2+ to copper metal.

questions.q: In a galvanic cell, oxidation takes place at the
questions.explanation: The anode is by definition the electrode where oxidation occurs, releasing electrons to the external circuit.

questions.q: How many electrons does one dichromate ion Cr2O7 2- gain when it is reduced to two Cr3+ ions in acidic solution?
questions.explanation: Each chromium changes from +6 to +3, gaining 3 electrons, so two chromium atoms gain 6 electrons.

questions.q: In the reaction 2Na + Cl2 → 2NaCl, identify the oxidising agent and the reducing agent.
questions.answer: Sodium is the reducing agent (it loses electrons, 0 to +1) and chlorine is the oxidising agent (it gains electrons, 0 to -1).
keyPoints: Na oxidised from 0 to +1: reducing agent
Cl2 reduced from 0 to -1: oxidising agent
Electrons move from Na to Cl
questions.explanation: The species that is oxidised acts as the reducing agent, and the species reduced is the oxidising agent.

questions.q: Calculate the oxidation number of oxygen in OF2 and explain why it is not -2.
questions.answer: +2. Fluorine is more electronegative than oxygen, so fluorine is -1 and the oxygen balances with +2.
keyPoints: Fluorine is more electronegative than oxygen
questions.explanation: Oxygen shows -2 only when bonded to elements less electronegative than itself.

questions.q: In sodium hydride, NaH, hydrogen is present as
questions.explanation: NaH is an ionic hydride made of Na+ and H- ions, since hydrogen gains an electron from the metal.

questions.q: What is the chemical formula of quicklime?
questions.explanation: Quicklime is calcium oxide, CaO, made by heating limestone.

questions.q: What is the formula of plaster of Paris?
questions.explanation: Plaster of Paris is calcium sulphate hemihydrate, obtained by heating gypsum (CaSO4·2H2O) at about 393 K.

questions.q: The reactivity of alkali metals towards water increases in the order
questions.explanation: Reactivity increases down the group as ionisation enthalpy decreases, so lithium reacts slowly and caesium explosively.

questions.q: Hard water does not give a good lather with soap because
options: Ca2+ and Mg2+ ions react with soap to form an insoluble scum
it has a low boiling point
questions.explanation: Soap (sodium stearate and similar salts) forms insoluble calcium and magnesium salts, which separate as scum.

questions.q: Which method is used for the laboratory preparation of dihydrogen?
options: Granulated zinc with dilute hydrochloric acid
questions.explanation: Zn + 2HCl → ZnCl2 + H2; copper is less reactive than hydrogen and does not react with dilute HCl.

questions.q: Unlike the carbonates of the other alkali metals, lithium carbonate
options: decomposes on heating to give Li2O and CO2
questions.explanation: The small Li+ ion polarises the carbonate ion strongly, so Li2CO3 decomposes on heating while other alkali carbonates are stable.

questions.q: Why do alkaline earth metals have higher melting points than alkali metals of the same period?
questions.answer: Each alkaline earth atom contributes two valence electrons and forms a smaller 2+ ion, so metallic bonding is stronger than in the alkali metals, which contribute one electron.
keyPoints: Smaller atoms and higher nuclear charge
questions.explanation: Stronger metallic bonds need more energy to break, so melting points are higher.

questions.q: Explain why ice floats on water.
questions.answer: In ice, hydrogen bonds hold water molecules in an open cage-like structure with empty spaces, so ice has a lower density than liquid water.
keyPoints: Each water molecule is hydrogen-bonded to four others in ice
questions.explanation: When ice melts the open structure partly collapses, so liquid water is denser.

questions.q: Which is the most abundant metal in the Earth's crust?
questions.explanation: Aluminium makes up about 8% of the Earth's crust by mass, more than any other metal.

questions.q: Quartz is a crystalline form of
questions.explanation: Quartz is crystalline silica, SiO2.

questions.q: Dry ice is
questions.explanation: Dry ice is solid CO2, which sublimes directly into gas at about -78 °C.

questions.q: Silicones are polymers whose backbone consists of repeating units of
questions.explanation: Silicones have an alternating silicon-oxygen chain with organic groups attached to silicon.

questions.q: Which compound is commonly called inorganic benzene?
questions.explanation: Borazine, B3N3H6, has a planar six-membered ring of alternating B and N atoms, similar to benzene.

questions.q: How many three-centre two-electron (banana) bonds are present in diborane, B2H6?
questions.explanation: Two bridging hydrogens each link the two boron atoms through a three-centre two-electron bond; the four terminal B-H bonds are ordinary.

questions.q: CCl4 is not hydrolysed by water, whereas SiCl4 is hydrolysed readily. This is because
options: silicon has vacant 3d orbitals that can accept a lone pair from water, but carbon has no d orbitals
carbon is more electronegative than silicon and attracts water
silicon forms stronger bonds with chlorine than carbon does
questions.explanation: Silicon can expand its coordination number using 3d orbitals, so water can attack it; carbon, having no d orbitals in its second shell, cannot.

questions.q: Write the equation showing that aluminium reacts with sodium hydroxide solution, and state the property it demonstrates.
questions.answer: 2Al + 2NaOH + 6H2O → 2Na[Al(OH)4] + 3H2. Aluminium is amphoteric, as it also reacts with acids.
keyPoints: Aluminium reacts with both acids and bases: amphoteric
questions.explanation: Reacting with both acids and strong alkalis shows amphoteric behaviour.

questions.q: Why does carbon show catenation to a much greater extent than other group 14 elements?
questions.answer: The C-C bond is very strong because of small size of carbon, and carbon forms stable bonds with itself, whereas bond enthalpies decrease down the group.
keyPoints: Small size gives strong C-C bonds
Bond enthalpy decreases from C to Pb
questions.explanation: The high C-C bond enthalpy (about 348 kJ/mol) makes long stable chains possible.

questions.q: Isomers are compounds that have the same molecular formula but different
questions.explanation: Isomers share a molecular formula but differ in the structural or spatial arrangement of atoms.

questions.q: Successive members of a homologous series differ by
questions.explanation: Each member differs from the next by one -CH2- unit.

questions.q: How many carbon atoms are present in the compound 2,2-dimethylbutane?
questions.explanation: The parent chain butane has 4 carbons, and the two methyl groups add 2 more, giving 6.

questions.q: What is the IUPAC name of CH3-CH(CH3)-CH2-CH3?
questions.explanation: The longest chain has four carbons, and the methyl is on carbon 2 when numbered from the nearer end.

questions.q: Which of the following is an electrophile?
questions.explanation: NO2+ is electron-deficient and accepts an electron pair; the others have lone pairs and act as nucleophiles.

questions.q: How many hyperconjugation structures can be written for the ethyl carbocation, CH3CH2+?
questions.explanation: Hyperconjugation involves the C-H bonds on the carbon next to the positive centre, and the CH3 group has three such bonds.

questions.q: Which of the following groups shows a +M (positive mesomeric) effect?
questions.explanation: The -NH2 group has a lone pair on nitrogen that can be donated into the pi system; the other groups withdraw electrons.

questions.q: What type of isomerism is shown by butan-1-ol and butan-2-ol?
questions.answer: Position isomerism, because the -OH group is on different carbon atoms of the same carbon chain.
keyPoints: Different position of the functional group
questions.explanation: Both are C4H10O and have a four-carbon chain, but -OH is on carbon 1 in one and carbon 2 in the other.

questions.q: Describe how nitrogen in an organic compound is detected by Lassaigne's test.
questions.answer: The compound is fused with sodium to give sodium cyanide; the extract is boiled with iron(II) sulphate and acidified, and Prussian blue colour shows nitrogen.
keyPoints: Add FeSO4 and then acidify with dilute acid
questions.explanation: Covalent nitrogen is converted into the ionic cyanide, which is then detected as the iron complex.

questions.q: Which is the simplest alkane?
questions.explanation: Methane, CH4, has one carbon atom and is the first member of the alkane series.

questions.q: Alkenes can show geometrical (cis-trans) isomerism because of
options: restricted rotation about the C=C double bond
free rotation about C-C single bonds
questions.explanation: The pi bond prevents rotation around the double bond, so different spatial arrangements of groups are fixed.

questions.q: When ethyne is passed through a red-hot iron tube at about 873 K, the product is
questions.explanation: Three molecules of ethyne polymerise (cyclic trimerisation) to give benzene.

questions.q: Partial hydrogenation of but-2-yne using Lindlar's catalyst gives mainly
questions.explanation: Lindlar's catalyst (poisoned palladium) adds hydrogen to the same face of the triple bond and stops at the alkene, giving the cis isomer.

questions.q: In the presence of a peroxide, HBr adds to propene to give mainly
questions.explanation: The peroxide effect (Kharasch) causes anti-Markovnikov addition via a free radical mechanism, putting bromine on the terminal carbon.

questions.q: Which reagent combination is used for the nitration of benzene?
questions.explanation: The mixture generates the nitronium ion, NO2+, which is the attacking electrophile.

questions.q: Reductive ozonolysis of but-2-ene gives
questions.explanation: The double bond between C2 and C3 is cleaved, so each CH3-CH= half becomes CH3CHO.

questions.q: Write the balanced equation for the complete combustion of propane.
keyPoints: Products are carbon dioxide and water
questions.explanation: Carbon balance gives 3 CO2, hydrogen balance gives 4 H2O, and oxygen then totals 10 atoms, so 5 O2.

questions.q: Explain why the -OH group on benzene directs an incoming electrophile to the ortho and para positions while the -NO2 group directs to the meta position.
questions.answer: -OH donates electron density to the ring by resonance (+M), increasing it at ortho and para positions; -NO2 withdraws electrons (-M, -I), lowering density mostly at ortho and para, so meta is least deactivated.
keyPoints: Electron density pattern decides the position of attack
questions.explanation: Electrophiles attack the position of highest electron density, which differs for donor and acceptor substituents.
